_about: Everything a car owner, and the owner's agent, would want to do with a car,
and where OmaCar stands on each. doc/ROADMAP.md holds the argument; this
file holds the list, because a list of two hundred things is exactly the
part of a roadmap that goes quietly wrong when it lives in prose.
`omacar roadmap --check` validates every entry, and `omacar roadmap`
counts them into the generated block of doc/ROADMAP.md. Nothing here is
counted by hand, and nothing here is executed.
FIELDS
id        stable, lowercase, dotted: `<area>.<what>`. Never reuse one.
domain    one of `domains` below.
title     what it is, in the words a driver would use.
user      what a person wants from it.
agent     what the owner's agent does with it.
status    shipped | building | next | later | research.
shipped   the files in `evidence` are tracked by git and do
what the entry says, on the cars the notes name.
building  started, and not yet true end to end. Work on
another branch cites the files on this one that
it lands in or replaces, and says so in notes.
next      sequenced in the Next phase of doc/ROADMAP.md.
later     wanted, not yet sequenced.
research  nobody knows yet whether it can be done well.
tier      the safety class, in lib/modes.py's language:
none      sends nothing to the car.
read      asks the car, and changes nothing in it.
write     changes something stored in the car.
actuate   moves something on the car.
gate      required for write and actuate, allowed for read: the key in
lib/modes.py ACTIONS that decides it. The check refuses an
action no mode allows -- reprogramming and guessing routine
identifiers are not capabilities, they are refusals.
needs     hardware beyond the computer running OmaCar, from `hardware`.
depends   ids of capabilities this one cannot work without. A shipped
capability may only depend on shipped ones.
evidence  repository paths that implement it. Every path must be
tracked by git; shipped and building need at least one.
notes     which cars and adapters it realistically works on, what it
cannot do, and anything a reader would otherwise assume.
REFUSALS AND WARNINGS
The owner decides; the app and the agent inform and warn before acting
(doc/ROADMAP.md, the governing principle). `refusals` are the few
exceptions the owner has confirmed, and `warnings` are guards the owner
has decided to be able to accept once the risk is stated. Every action
lib/modes.py refuses in every mode must appear in one list or the other,
so the code and the owner's decisions cannot quietly disagree. A gate
named by a refusal can never be a capability. A gate named by a warning
that the code still refuses may be planned but not shipped. Each title
must also appear in doc/ROADMAP.md's prose.
ADDING ONE. Pick the domain, write the four sentences a person and an
agent would need, set status honestly (read the code before writing
`shipped`), and run `omacar roadmap --check`. It names every problem.

obd-usb.title: Wired USB OBD-II adapter, ELM327- or STN-based
obd-usb.notes: The only transport OmaCar speaks today. OBDLink SX and EX are the adapters it was developed on (lib/connect.py knows both defaults). Cheap clones answer to the same commands and often lie about their firmware version; see the hardware guide.

obd-wireless.title: Bluetooth or Wi-Fi OBD-II adapter
obd-wireless.notes: Not supported yet. The cheapest adapters people already own are these.

j2534.title: SAE J2534 pass-thru device
j2534.notes: A published standard, and the transport professional hardware already speaks. Not supported yet.

can-usb.title: SocketCAN USB-to-CAN interface
can-usb.notes: CANable-class, native on Linux. Not supported yet.

usb-camera.title: USB cameras for the road
usb-camera.notes: Action cameras in webcam mode (DJI Osmo Action 4, Insta360 Ace Pro) and a Logitech C920 are the owner's set. What the action cameras offer on Linux is measured, not assumed.

ir-camera.title: Infrared cabin camera
ir-camera.notes: Needed for drowsiness detection at night. An ELP 1080p with IR LEDs and a 3.6 mm lens is the recommendation in the cameras design; not yet bought.

gnss.title: u-blox NEO-M9V GNSS receiver and a roof antenna
gnss.notes: Decided with the owner on 2026-09-27/28. The NEO-M9V does untethered and automotive dead reckoning (u-blox, checked 2026-09-28).

rtl-sdr.title: RTL-SDR USB radio receiver
rtl-sdr.notes: For tyre sensors. The RTL-SDR Blog V4 reached end of line in May 2026; the V4L is its replacement (rtl-sdr.com, checked 2026-09-28).

carplay-dongle.title: Carlinkit CarPlay / Android Auto adapter
carplay-dongle.notes: The phone screen's driver speaks its protocol and has never been run against one.

aux-cable.title: 3.5 mm AUX cable into the car's audio
aux-cable.notes: How sound reaches the owner's car (decided 2026-09-28).

tablet-camera.title: The tablet's own camera
tablet-camera.notes: For photographs of parts and documents. Browsers only allow it on a secure origin, which loopback is.

tpms-tool.title: TPMS trigger and programming tool
tpms-tool.notes: A 125 kHz trigger that wakes and programs direct TPMS sensors. Out of reach of a USB radio, which can only listen.

internet.title: An internet connection
internet.notes: A phone hotspot in the car. Everything marked with it degrades to saying so when offline, and nothing else needs it.

home-machine.title: An always-on Omarchy machine at home, on the same tailnet
home-machine.notes: Pushes documents to the car, relays Work sessions, and is where a backup would live. No cloud host.

claude.title: A Claude subscription, logged in through Claude Code
claude.notes: The advisor and Work run on the owner's own subscription through the local `claude` CLI. Not hardware, and listed here because it is a thing you must have.

refusals.title: Writes that disable emissions controls
refusals.why: Federal law: Clean Air Act s203(a)(3) prohibits rendering an emission control inoperative, and EPA's 2020 enforcement policy says that covers software.

refusals.title: Reprogramming that needs a manufacturer-signed image
refusals.why: This tool cannot produce a signed image, and an interrupted transfer leaves a module with no firmware at all.

refusals.title: Writes to the car while it is moving
refusals.why: The risk falls on other people on the road, who did not choose it.

warnings.title: Guessing a routine identifier
warnings.risk: A routine is something a module runs. A guessed number can spin a fan, cycle an ABS pump or retract a parking brake with a wheel off.

warnings.title: Writing or sweeping below 12.2 V
warnings.risk: A long session on a low battery can trip warning lights (a 25-minute key-on sweep tripped the ABS warning) or leave the car unable to start.

warnings.title: An agent raising its own tier, promoting its own finding, or sending a write
warnings.risk: An agent can be wrong with confidence, and a finding it promotes itself becomes data other owners trust.

warnings.title: Plugins breaking the driving-screen rules
warnings.risk: Text entry, small targets and motion on a screen in view of the driver take attention off the road. Writes while moving stay refused whatever is accepted.

capabilities.title: Read the engine computer's trouble codes
capabilities.user: Know why the check engine light is on without paying a shop to plug in.
capabilities.agent: Reads stored, pending and permanent codes and reports them with their status.
capabilities.notes: Any OBD-II car on a protocol the adapter speaks: US 1996 on, EU petrol 2001 and diesel 2004 on. Proven on one car, a 2015 Honda CR-Z on CAN 29/500. Generic OBD-II reaches the powertrain module only.

capabilities.title: Every code explained in plain words
capabilities.user: Understand what a code means, how serious it is, and whether the car is safe to drive.
capabilities.agent: Explains a code from its structure and, for the deeply written ones, gives ranked causes, symptoms and tests.
capabilities.notes: Any code decodes structurally. A small set carries deep entries; the IMA entries in dtc.json are unsourced and are a standing claim in doc/roadmap.json.

capabilities.title: Freeze frame, attached to its code
capabilities.user: See what the engine was doing at the moment a fault set.
capabilities.agent: Reads the freeze frame and files it with the code it belongs to.
capabilities.notes: Any OBD-II car on a protocol the adapter speaks: US 1996 on, EU petrol 2001 and diesel 2004 on. Proven on one car, a 2015 Honda CR-Z on CAN 29/500.

capabilities.title: The live values that tell causes apart
capabilities.user: For a stored code, see only the readings that decide between its likely causes.
capabilities.agent: Resolves a code's discriminating values against this car's live data and Mode 06 results.
capabilities.notes: Only for codes with a deep entry in dtc.json.

capabilities.title: A full scan, filed as one report
capabilities.user: One page that says which parts of the car are holding faults, kept in the car's record.
capabilities.agent: Runs the scan, files it in the record book and summarises it.
capabilities.notes: On a real car the report honestly lists one module, the engine, because a generic adapter reaches only that. The simulator shows the multi-module version.

capabilities.title: Scan every module the car has
capabilities.user: Faults from ABS, airbags, body, steering and hybrid systems, not just the engine.
capabilities.agent: Walks every module discovery found and reads each one's faults over UDS 0x19.
capabilities.notes: Realistic on CAN cars that speak UDS on the diagnostic port, roughly 2008 on. Pre-UDS makes need manufacturer protocols. Security gateways usually still allow reads.

capabilities.title: Read a module's faults and fault catalogue over UDS
capabilities.user: See the codes a manufacturer module can set, not only the ones it has set.
capabilities.agent: Asks a module for its stored codes and its catalogue of every code it can set (0x19 0x0A).
capabilities.notes: Needs the module's header. Validated on the CR-Z's two hybrid controllers; any UDS-on-CAN module should answer.

capabilities.title: Watch fault status change across a drive
capabilities.user: Tell a monitor that has not run from a fault that is really there.
capabilities.agent: Samples fault status through a drive and reports which monitors ran.
capabilities.notes: On the CR-Z every hybrid code so far reads status 0x40, not run. The screen leads with that.

capabilities.title: Clear codes after a repair
capabilities.user: Turn the light off after fixing the fault, knowing what clearing also resets.
capabilities.agent: Proposes a clear after a verified repair; the owner arms and confirms it.
capabilities.notes: Generic Mode 04 on any OBD-II car. Refused while moving, for good. Refused below 12.2 V today; that becomes a warning the owner can accept (decided 2026-09-28). Clearing also resets readiness, which the screen says first.

capabilities.title: Guided diagnosis for a stored code
capabilities.user: What it means, the usual causes in order, and what to test next, for this car.
capabilities.agent: Reasons over this car's freeze frame, trims, Mode 06 and history and returns findings that cite their evidence.
capabilities.notes: Any car with data on file. Findings whose evidence keys are not in the bundle are dropped before display.

capabilities.title: A symptom with no code
capabilities.user: The car shudders at 40 mph and there is no light: what should I record?
capabilities.agent: Turns a described symptom into a recording plan and reads the recording back.
capabilities.notes: The `symptom` and `recording` kinds in lib/ai.py.

capabilities.title: Live data, at gauge speed
capabilities.user: Watch coolant, trims, load and speed live while the car runs.
capabilities.agent: Reads the live snapshot and the readings catalogue so its numbers match the screen's.
capabilities.notes: Any OBD-II car on a protocol the adapter speaks: US 1996 on, EU petrol 2001 and diesel 2004 on. Proven on one car, a 2015 Honda CR-Z on CAN 29/500. Tiered polling at about 10 Hz for the fast group.

capabilities.title: Several channels on one time axis
capabilities.user: Catch the misfire that happens once a minute by seeing channels together with a cursor.
capabilities.agent: Picks the channels that matter for a question and reads values at an instant.
capabilities.notes: Any OBD-II car on a protocol the adapter speaks: US 1996 on, EU petrol 2001 and diesel 2004 on. Proven on one car, a 2015 Honda CR-Z on CAN 29/500.

capabilities.title: Replay a drive and export it
capabilities.user: Scrub back to the moment something happened and read every channel, or take it into a spreadsheet.
capabilities.agent: Reads a recorded drive at any instant and exports CSV for analysis.
capabilities.notes: About 1 Hz history from the vehicle database.

capabilities.title: Trends and snapshots
capabilities.user: See what is drifting toward a limit, and freeze the whole state to compare later.
capabilities.agent: Draws a line through repeated measurements and says when a margin will run out.
capabilities.notes: Only as good as the history on file: a car seen once has no trend.

capabilities.title: Capture an intermittent fault unattended
capabilities.user: When something goes wrong on a hill, have the evidence waiting rather than a rumour.
capabilities.agent: The watchdog freezes a full snapshot the moment a rule fires and links it to the alert.

capabilities.title: Tell me while it is going wrong
capabilities.user: A notification for overheating, a charging system that stopped, low fuel or over-revving, during the drive.
capabilities.agent: Watches live data with debounced, hysteretic rules and files alerts it can read back.
capabilities.notes: Rules use generic PIDs, so they work wherever live data does.

capabilities.title: Functional tests with a live trace
capabilities.user: Switch the fan, purge valve, EGR, A/C clutch or fuel pump on to prove it works.
capabilities.agent: Proposes the test that would discriminate between causes; the owner runs it.
capabilities.notes: Works on the simulator. On a real car only a validated actuator entry reaches a button, and no car has one yet. Only 0x2F leaves the module; release is unconditional.

capabilities.title: A report a mechanic or buyer will take seriously
capabilities.user: A printable page, or one self-contained file, of what the car arrived with.
capabilities.agent: Builds the report and says which parts were measured and which were typed.
capabilities.notes: Prints to PDF from the browser.

capabilities.title: Service bulletins and known issues for this model
capabilities.user: Know what the manufacturer has already told dealers about a problem like mine.
capabilities.agent: Looks up published manufacturer communications for the decoded model and cites them.
capabilities.notes: NHTSA publishes manufacturer communications for US vehicles. Licensed repair information (ALLDATA, Mitchell1) is not cloned, ever.

capabilities.title: Say plainly when a security gateway blocks us
capabilities.user: Know that a refusal is the car's gateway, not a broken tool.
capabilities.agent: Recognises gateway refusals and explains what access would be needed.
capabilities.notes: FCA SGW and its equivalents need authenticated access for writes; reads are often unaffected. Authenticating is a separate, later question.

capabilities.title: Lab scope alongside the scan data
capabilities.user: See an injector or crank sensor waveform next to the live data that explains it.
capabilities.agent: Reads captures from a scope the owner already owns and lines them up with bus data.
capabilities.notes: No scope is shipped or planned as hardware. Integration with one people own.

capabilities.title: Readiness monitors
capabilities.user: Know whether the car will be turned away at the smog station for incomplete monitors.
capabilities.agent: Reads monitor state and says which are incomplete.
capabilities.notes: Any OBD-II car on a protocol the adapter speaks: US 1996 on, EU petrol 2001 and diesel 2004 on. Proven on one car, a 2015 Honda CR-Z on CAN 29/500.

capabilities.title: Why a monitor will not complete
capabilities.user: Not just two monitors incomplete, but what is stopping them and which fix unblocks both.
capabilities.agent: Connects incomplete monitors to the codes and conditions that abort them.
capabilities.notes: Explanations exist for the generic monitors.

capabilities.title: On-board test results, with the margin to each limit
capabilities.user: See how close each self-test is to failing, not only whether it passed.
capabilities.agent: Reads Mode 06 and reports margin to limit per test.
capabilities.notes: Every OBD-II car has Mode 06; CAN cars report it in a standard shape, older ones vary by maker.

capabilities.title: A test's margin, over months
capabilities.user: A catalyst at 95% of its limit and climbing is a failure with a date on it.
capabilities.agent: Trends Mode 06 margins across scans and projects when one crosses.
capabilities.notes: Needs repeated scans of the same car, which a tool that lives in the car gets and a workshop tool does not.

capabilities.title: A drive cycle to get monitors ready
capabilities.user: After a battery change or a clear, get the monitors complete before the test.
capabilities.agent: Tells the driver which conditions each incomplete monitor still needs.
capabilities.notes: Written as an owner procedure at confidence `reported`: nobody has yet verified it on a real car.

capabilities.title: Will it pass? A pre-inspection verdict
capabilities.user: Walk into the test knowing the answer, under your state's rules for your model year.
capabilities.agent: Combines the lamp, confirmed codes and readiness against the allowance that applies.
capabilities.notes: Allowances differ by state and model year; each rule must cite its source rather than be recalled.

capabilities.title: Permanent codes, and how to retire them
capabilities.user: Know why a code survives clearing and what drive retires it.
capabilities.agent: Reads Mode 0A and explains the drive that clears a permanent code.
capabilities.notes: Mode 0A exists on 2010-on US cars; older cars do not report it.

capabilities.title: A service book that counts down
capabilities.user: Know what is due by mileage and by time, whichever comes first.
capabilities.agent: Reads what is due and proposes the next service from the book.
capabilities.notes: Starts from a conservative generic schedule with everything due until told otherwise. The handbook wins.

capabilities.title: The odometer, which OBD-II does not report
capabilities.user: Keep an accurate mileage without the car reporting one.
capabilities.agent: Advances the owner's reading by distance driven and flags when it needs re-setting.
capabilities.notes: PID 0xA6 exists in later standards and almost nothing implements it.

capabilities.title: A service history built from receipts
capabilities.user: Photograph a receipt and have the book know the oil was changed.
capabilities.agent: Extracts what was done from a document and proposes book entries the owner accepts.
capabilities.notes: Extraction is labelled as extracted and never overwrites typed fields.

capabilities.title: Owner procedures: the jobs that need no tool
capabilities.user: Oil-life reset, TPMS calibration, key fob resync: buttons and menus, explained.
capabilities.agent: Finds the procedure for this make and walks the owner through it.
capabilities.notes: Mostly Honda so far, all at confidence `reported`. Nothing is sent to the car.

capabilities.title: Reset oil life over the bus
capabilities.user: Reset the service reminder from the app on cars with no button sequence.
capabilities.agent: Runs the published routine for this make after the owner confirms.
capabilities.notes: Next, after the IMA drives (decided 2026-09-28). Per-make routine definitions, confirmed on a real car before they leave `unverified`.

capabilities.title: Service resets from published definitions
capabilities.user: The resets that force a shop visit, done at home: the highest value per hour on this roadmap.
capabilities.agent: Chooses the published definition for this car and states its preconditions and consequences.
capabilities.notes: The routine-control path and the definition format exist; only two generic clears are defined. Routine identifiers are never guessed.

capabilities.title: Electronic parking brake service mode
capabilities.user: Retract the rear calipers to change pads without a scan tool.
capabilities.agent: Runs the make's published retract and re-apply routines, never with a wheel off and the car unsupported.
capabilities.notes: Often available in an extended session without SecurityAccess. Per-make.

capabilities.title: Steering angle sensor calibration
capabilities.user: Recalibrate after an alignment so stability control trusts the wheel again.
capabilities.agent: Runs the published routine and checks the sensor reads centre afterwards.
capabilities.notes: Per-make.

capabilities.title: Battery registration
capabilities.user: Tell the car a new battery is fitted so it charges it correctly.
capabilities.agent: Runs the make's registration routine after a battery change.
capabilities.notes: Mostly European cars. Per-make.

capabilities.title: Throttle and idle relearn
capabilities.user: Fix a hunting idle after cleaning a throttle body or disconnecting the battery.
capabilities.agent: Runs the routine where one is published, or the owner procedure where it is a drive sequence.
capabilities.notes: Honda's idle relearn is already an owner procedure; the routine version is per-make.

capabilities.title: Diesel particulate filter regeneration
capabilities.user: Force a regeneration instead of paying for one.
capabilities.agent: Runs a published regeneration routine only with the car parked, in the open, and the owner watching.
capabilities.notes: Diesels only. Exhaust gets very hot; the precondition text matters as much as the bytes.

capabilities.title: Read the car's own oil-life percentage
capabilities.user: See the Maintenance Minder's own figure, not only the book's estimate.
capabilities.agent: Finds and validates the identifier that carries it.
capabilities.notes: Honda's identifier for it is unknown. Found by discovery or by a community signal set.

capabilities.title: Reminders when something is due
capabilities.user: Be told a service is coming before the light comes on.
capabilities.agent: Sends a reminder through the channels the owner set up.

capabilities.title: Repair information, linked and annotated
capabilities.user: Get to the right procedure and keep my own notes on the car.
capabilities.agent: Links out to the owner's repair information and files notes against the vehicle.
capabilities.notes: Licensed repair content is never cloned. Linking out and owner notes only.

capabilities.title: Is this quote reasonable?
capabilities.user: Photograph a shop estimate and understand what it is for and whether it matches the fault.
capabilities.agent: Reads the estimate against this car's codes and history and asks the questions a good mechanic would.
capabilities.notes: Labour-time databases are licensed. Without one this can explain, not price.

capabilities.title: Community repair guides
capabilities.user: Step-by-step jobs with photos, written by owners of the same model.
capabilities.agent: Finds the guide for this car and this fault and checks its preconditions.
capabilities.notes: The procedure format and its confidence ladder already exist to carry them.

capabilities.title: Photographs filed against what they show
capabilities.user: Keep the picture of the perished hose with the code it explains.
capabilities.agent: Attaches photographs to codes and systems and reads them back for a report.

capabilities.title: What the hybrid modules can measure
capabilities.user: See the hybrid system's own fault catalogue, honestly labelled as not-run where it is.
capabilities.agent: Assembles the catalogues into a map of what each hybrid module monitors, with the not-run caveat first.
capabilities.notes: The 2015 CR-Z only. The procedure is model-shaped and should carry to any hybrid.

capabilities.title: Hybrid battery remaining life, from the generic PID
capabilities.user: One honest number for the hybrid battery, where the car publishes it.
capabilities.agent: Reads PID 0x5B where the car's bitmap claims it and says when there is no answer.
capabilities.notes: Home's tile reads it and says 'Waiting for the car' until it answers. It is in the CR-Z's supported bitmap and has never been polled: a standing claim.

capabilities.title: Live IMA pack voltage, current, charge and temperature
capabilities.user: See what the hybrid system is doing: assist, regen, charge, heat.
capabilities.agent: Validates each IMA channel against a trusted one before it may drive a gauge.
capabilities.notes: No live IMA quantity has ever been captured on the CR-Z. The 2026-09-29 discovery drives are the next attempt.

capabilities.title: Cell-block balance and pack health
capabilities.user: Know whether the IMA battery is failing before a dealer quotes a replacement.
capabilities.agent: Reads block voltages and judges spread under load.
capabilities.notes: Depends on block voltages crossing the diagnostic port at all, which is unknown on the CR-Z.

capabilities.title: Hybrid battery capacity over years
capabilities.user: Watch the pack age, and compare it with other cars of the same model and age.
capabilities.agent: Trends capacity estimates and, with consent, compares against the community.
capabilities.notes: Was a cloud feature in the old Phase 3. Now owner-held data, shared only by choice.

capabilities.title: Hybrid data for other makes
capabilities.user: Toyota, Lexus, Ford and Hyundai hybrid owners get their pack data too.
capabilities.agent: Imports community signal sets for the model and validates them on the car.
capabilities.notes: Community signal sets exist for many hybrids; each is a lead until validated here.

capabilities.title: EV battery state of health
capabilities.user: Know an EV's real remaining capacity before buying or selling it.
capabilities.agent: Reads the model's state-of-health signals and explains what they measure.
capabilities.notes: Manufacturer-specific. Leads from community sets, validated per model.

capabilities.title: Charging sessions and cost
capabilities.user: What charging costs, at home and away.
capabilities.agent: Logs sessions from the car's own signals and prices them.
capabilities.notes: EVs and plug-in hybrids.

capabilities.title: A used-hybrid check before buying
capabilities.user: Plug into a car for sale and know whether its hybrid battery is sound.
capabilities.agent: Runs a short read-only check and writes a plain verdict with its evidence.

capabilities.title: 12 V system voltage, live
capabilities.user: See the battery and charging voltage at a glance.
capabilities.agent: Reads control-module voltage and says whether the car is charging.
capabilities.notes: Any OBD-II car on a protocol the adapter speaks: US 1996 on, EU petrol 2001 and diesel 2004 on. Proven on one car, a 2015 Honda CR-Z on CAN 29/500.

capabilities.title: Warn when the charging system stops
capabilities.user: Know the alternator stopped charging while there is still time to get home.
capabilities.agent: Raises an alert and captures the evidence.

capabilities.title: Protect the battery during long sessions
capabilities.user: Never flatten the battery, or trip a warning light, while the tool is working.
capabilities.agent: Refuses writes and sweeps below the floor and says why.
capabilities.notes: The 12.2 V floor exists because a 25-minute key-on sweep tripped an ABS warning. Decided 2026-09-28: it becomes a warning the owner can accept, with that risk stated. The code still refuses until safe.accept-risk lands.

capabilities.title: Replacing the 12 V battery without losing settings
capabilities.user: What to note before, and what to relearn after.
capabilities.agent: Walks the checklist and schedules the relearns the car will need.
capabilities.notes: Confidence `reported`.

capabilities.title: Cranking voltage and battery health trend
capabilities.user: Know the battery is weakening months before it fails on a cold morning.
capabilities.agent: Captures the dip at each start and trends it.
capabilities.notes: ATRV reads the adapter pin, and an ELM327's sample rate may be too slow for the dip. Measure before promising.

capabilities.title: A guided charging-system test
capabilities.user: Test the alternator under load the way a shop would.
capabilities.agent: Guides loads on and off and judges the voltage response.
capabilities.notes: The owner switches the loads; nothing is commanded.

capabilities.title: Parked battery drain
capabilities.user: Find out why the battery is flat after a week parked.
capabilities.agent: Watches voltage while parked and reports the curve.

capabilities.agent: Uses Opus 5.5 for diagnosis and keeps Haiku for quick owner answers.
capabilities.notes: Task 9 of the foundation plan; lib/ai.py still names Sonnet 5 on this branch.

capabilities.title: Voice: ask, and move the screen
capabilities.user: Talk to the car's assistant and have the right screen come up.
capabilities.agent: Moves the screen on a spoken request, once, and says who asked.
capabilities.notes: Cannot reach the car through this path.

capabilities.title: Plugins: commands, screens, hooks and data
capabilities.user: Extend OmaCar without forking it.
capabilities.agent: Writes a plugin directory with a manifest; hooks get JSON on stdin.
capabilities.notes: A plugin is code you are running. There is no sandbox, and the docs say so.

capabilities.title: A map of the whole car an agent can read
capabilities.user: My agent knows what exists, what is next and what it needs.
capabilities.agent: Reads doc/capabilities.json, picks a `next` item, and follows its depends and needs.
capabilities.notes: `omacar roadmap --list next` prints the candidates.

capabilities.title: An SDK for owners' agents
capabilities.user: My agent builds what I need for my car: a screen, a data source, a camera view.
capabilities.agent: Uses a documented contract: typed car data, the design tokens, the driving state, and declared permissions.
capabilities.notes: Covers car data, CarPlay, the interface, cameras and navigation, as decided 2026-09-27/28.

capabilities.title: Start a plugin in one command
capabilities.user: A working skeleton with a test, in the house style.
capabilities.agent: Scaffolds the plugin and its test, then runs the checks.

capabilities.title: Plugins declare what they need
capabilities.user: Know before installing whether a plugin reads, writes or commands the car.
capabilities.agent: Declares a tier; the server enforces lib/modes.py on the plugin's calls.
capabilities.notes: Today a plugin's command runs with the owner's full access.

capabilities.title: More events to hook
capabilities.user: Run my own automation when a drive starts, a service is due or a clip is locked.
capabilities.agent: Subscribes to the new events.
capabilities.notes: Today: on-fault, on-drive-end, on-scan.

capabilities.title: An agent carries out what the owner approved
capabilities.user: Tell my agent to do the job, confirm once on screen, and let it run it properly.
capabilities.agent: Runs an owner-approved write through the same gates a person uses.
capabilities.notes: The owner decides; the agent informs first. Writes while moving stay refused. The agent limits become warnings the owner can accept (decided 2026-09-28).

capabilities.title: Work: coding sessions from the car
capabilities.user: Continue work on my Omarchy machines from the car, by voice while driving.
capabilities.agent: Relays sessions on the owner's Claude subscription through his own box.
capabilities.notes: Decided 2026-09-28: a relay on the owner's machine, no cloud hosting. The tab is a placeholder.

capabilities.title: An advisor that works with no signal
capabilities.user: Guided diagnosis in a rural garage with no connection.
capabilities.agent: Falls back to a local model and says which model answered.
capabilities.notes: Whether a local model is good enough to be trusted here is the research question.

capabilities.title: Wired USB adapters
capabilities.user: Plug in a cable and have it found.
capabilities.agent: Finds the adapter, the right baud rate and the port lease.
capabilities.notes: ELM327 and STN chipsets on /dev/ttyUSB* or ttyACM*. OBDLink SX and EX are the tested pair.

capabilities.title: Plug in the adapter and the app appears
capabilities.user: No commands in the driveway.
capabilities.agent: Starts the daemon and the app when the adapter appears.

capabilities.title: A bench emulator
capabilities.user: Develop and learn without a car.
capabilities.agent: Runs scenarios against an emulated adapter and module.

capabilities.title: A whole simulated car
capabilities.user: See every screen working before buying anything.
capabilities.agent: Seeds a year of driving, faults and service on a simulated CR-Z, labelled SIMULATED.

capabilities.title: A tablet that lives in the car
capabilities.user: A second-hand tablet or laptop that does not suspend, blank or overheat on the dash.
capabilities.agent: Checks the machine is ready and names the command that fixes each gap.
capabilities.notes: Surface Pro 7+ is the reference. Heat on a dash in summer is only partly answered.

capabilities.title: Any tablet on the network as a display
capabilities.user: Use an old tablet as a second gauge screen.
capabilities.agent: Serves the gauge to the local network, read-only by default.
capabilities.notes: A browser reached over the LAN cannot use a camera; that is the browser's rule.

capabilities.title: A hardware guide, especially for older cars
capabilities.user: Know what to buy for my car, what the cheap stuff cannot do, and what I already own that works.
capabilities.agent: Recommends hardware from the car's year, protocol and the owner's goals, with dated prices.
capabilities.notes: Every price dated and sourced. Cheap ELM327 clones copy old firmware and misreport their version; the guide says what that breaks.

capabilities.title: Tell a good adapter from a bad clone
capabilities.user: Know my twenty-dollar adapter is the problem before blaming the car.
capabilities.agent: Probes the adapter's real capabilities and says which features it cannot support.

capabilities.title: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi adapters
capabilities.user: Use the cheap adapter I already bought.
capabilities.agent: Connects over RFCOMM or TCP and warns about latency.

capabilities.title: SocketCAN interfaces
capabilities.user: Native Linux CAN, faster than any ELM327.
capabilities.agent: Speaks ISO-TP over SocketCAN.
capabilities.notes: The natural partner to passive listening.

capabilities.title: J2534 pass-thru
capabilities.user: Use professional hardware I already own.
capabilities.agent: Drives a J2534 device through its published API.
capabilities.notes: Most J2534 drivers are Windows DLLs; Linux support is the real work.

capabilities.title: What of a Snap-on kit carries over
capabilities.user: Keep the probes and leads I already paid for.
capabilities.agent: Answers which accessories are reusable and which are not.

capabilities.title: Fitting the GNSS receiver
capabilities.user: Mount the antenna and wire the receiver once.
capabilities.agent: Checks fix quality and says when the antenna is badly placed.

capabilities.title: Powering the tablet from the car
capabilities.user: Keep it charged without a fire risk or a flat battery.
capabilities.agent: Reads the tablet's charge state and warns when car power is not enough.

capabilities.title: First run, safety first
capabilities.user: Know whether this is safe to plug into the car I drive to work tomorrow.
capabilities.agent: Explains what the tool will and will not send.

capabilities.title: The app explains itself in place
capabilities.user: Understand 'Mode 06' or 'STFT' where I see it.
capabilities.agent: Explains any term on screen in plain words.

capabilities.title: Demo mode that cannot touch the real car
capabilities.user: Show somebody the tool without their fingerprints on my car's record.
capabilities.agent: Runs a throwaway install with its own data.
capabilities.notes: Isolation is two environment variables, so there is nothing to forget.

capabilities.title: Every command, on the wallpaper
capabilities.user: Find the command I need without reading docs.
capabilities.agent: Generates the reference from the commands themselves.

capabilities.title: One press to get ready to drive
capabilities.user: Everything checked before leaving the driveway.
capabilities.agent: Runs the preflight and fixes what it safely can.

capabilities.title: Is anything watching my car?
capabilities.user: One screen that says what is running and when it last heard from the car.
capabilities.agent: Reads status and the adapter report.

capabilities.title: Install on Omarchy
capabilities.user: One script, and it works.
capabilities.agent: Runs the installer and reports what it set up.
capabilities.notes: Omarchy (Arch) only today.

capabilities.title: A guide for people who have never done this
capabilities.user: From 'I have a car and a laptop' to a first useful answer in minutes.
capabilities.agent: Walks the owner through hardware, install and a first scan.

capabilities.title: Onboarding for agents
capabilities.user: My agent learns the rules of this repository before it touches my car.
capabilities.agent: Reads one guide: the principles, the tiers, the MCP tools, the roadmap and how to test.

capabilities.title: Learn your car
capabilities.user: Short lessons: how OBD works, what codes mean, working safely.
capabilities.agent: Picks the lesson that fits the question the owner just asked.

capabilities.title: Beyond Omarchy
capabilities.user: Run it on the Linux laptop I already have.
capabilities.agent: Checks the dependencies and says what is missing.
capabilities.notes: The Omarchy integration is additive; the core is Python and a browser.

capabilities.title: The car in the Omarchy bar
capabilities.user: A steering wheel that fills in when the engine turns, and a panel behind it.
capabilities.agent: Reads the same rollup the bar reads.

capabilities.title: OmaCar in the Omarchy menu
capabilities.user: Scan, advise and start the watchdog from the menu.
capabilities.agent: Launches the same commands.

capabilities.title: OmaMenu
capabilities.user: A system-wide replacement for the Omarchy menu, touch-first.
capabilities.agent: Adds entries the owner asks for.
capabilities.notes: Step 5 of the reimagining.

capabilities.title: Wear the Omarchy theme
capabilities.user: The car screen in my desktop's colours, when I want that.
capabilities.agent: Maps the desktop theme onto the app's tokens.

capabilities.title: Background services that stay out of the way
capabilities.user: The car never slows the desktop down.
capabilities.agent: Runs every background job niced, restartable and visible.
capabilities.notes: Nice=10 because an unthrottled poll loop once crashed the compositor.

capabilities.title: Kiosk mode for the car
capabilities.user: The tablet boots to the car screen, full screen.
capabilities.agent: Starts and stops kiosk mode.

capabilities.title: The baby, from the road
capabilities.user: Is anything happening at home, on a screen already in view.
capabilities.agent: Reads the document the home machine pushes; never a live feed while moving.
capabilities.notes: Holds no credential. The home machine pushes over the tailnet.

capabilities.title: A daily report, when I am not looking
capabilities.user: What the car did and what is drifting, by mail or a phone notification.
capabilities.agent: Composes the report, redacted by default, and sends it through the owner's own channels.
capabilities.notes: Written and tested; nothing calls it yet, and there is no command or timer.

capabilities.title: Keep the record without filling the disk
capabilities.user: A year of driving that stays fast.
capabilities.agent: Rolls old samples into daily figures.

capabilities.title: Private pictures, synced from home
capabilities.user: Honda-badged art on the tablet without it ever entering git.
capabilities.agent: Copies private assets from the home machine over the tailnet and checks their manifest.

capabilities.title: The car's record on my own machines
capabilities.user: My data survives a reinstall and is readable at home.
capabilities.agent: Syncs per-VIN records to the owner's home machine over the tailnet.
capabilities.notes: Replaces the old Phase 3's cloud garage. No hosted service.

capabilities.title: Backups I control
capabilities.user: Never lose the car's history.
capabilities.agent: Backs up the records to a destination the owner chose.

capabilities.title: Your data, on your disk
capabilities.user: No account, no server, readable files.
capabilities.agent: Reads SQLite and JSON the owner owns.

capabilities.title: Privacy mode for photographs
capabilities.user: Post a screenshot without the VIN, plate or my name.
capabilities.agent: Masks identifiers on screen with a visible indicator.

capabilities.title: Nothing about me reaches a model
capabilities.user: My agent and my voice assistant never see my VIN, plate or name.
capabilities.agent: Receives an allowlisted snapshot; anything VIN-shaped is scrubbed by value.
capabilities.notes: An allowlist, not a denylist.

capabilities.title: Export everything
capabilities.user: Take all of my car's data with me in open formats.
capabilities.agent: Exports every record, document and recording.
capabilities.notes: CSV export of drives exists; a full archive does not.

capabilities.title: Forget a car completely
capabilities.user: When I sell it, nothing of it stays behind.
capabilities.agent: Removes every record of that car and says what it removed.
capabilities.notes: `omacar vehicle forget` sets the database aside as `.removed` and switches away. Drive logs, frontier records, photographs and documents keyed to that car stay on disk.

capabilities.title: Location history I control
capabilities.user: Decide how long trip traces are kept, and delete them.
capabilities.agent: Applies the owner's retention rules.
capabilities.notes: Arrives with the receiver, not after it.

capabilities.title: Camera recordings I control
capabilities.user: A cabin camera that watches my eyes and keeps only what I choose.
capabilities.agent: Keeps the loop inside its budget and keeps locked clips only.
capabilities.notes: Being built on redesign/cameras.

capabilities.title: Every colour readable
capabilities.user: Text I can read in daylight, held to a standard.
capabilities.agent: Checks contrast against WCAG AA.

capabilities.title: Targets a thumb can hit
capabilities.user: Nothing too small to tap in a moving car.
capabilities.agent: Keeps touch targets at 48 px, 56 px on a coarse pointer.

capabilities.title: Type readable at arm's length
capabilities.user: Choose a typeface and size that I can read.
capabilities.agent: Sets the font on request.

capabilities.title: Night looks
capabilities.user: A dim or red screen that does not ruin night vision.
capabilities.agent: Switches look on request or by time.

capabilities.title: Simplified mode
capabilities.user: Four things that matter, in plain words.
capabilities.agent: Answers at the level the owner chose.

capabilities.title: Charts colour-blind people can read
capabilities.user: Tell every line on a chart apart.
capabilities.agent: Chooses separable colours.

capabilities.title: A big button that types what you say
capabilities.user: Dictate without a keyboard.
capabilities.agent: Receives dictated text like typed text.

capabilities.title: Screen reader support
capabilities.user: Use the app without seeing it.
capabilities.agent: Relies on labelled controls.
capabilities.notes: Not audited. Nobody has run the app under a screen reader.

capabilities.title: Other languages
capabilities.user: The app in Spanish, and more.
capabilities.agent: Answers in the owner's language.
capabilities.notes: Snap-on's entry tools ship English and Spanish.

capabilities.title: Alerts that do not rely on sound
capabilities.user: Every audio alert also visible.
capabilities.agent: Pairs every sound with a visual state.

capabilities.title: Five tabs a driver would name
capabilities.user: Home, Navigation, Cameras, Vehicle and Agent, with every old screen one tap away.
capabilities.agent: Opens any screen by name.
capabilities.notes: Placeholders say what each coming screen will do and which step builds it.

capabilities.title: Home
capabilities.user: Speed, the car, the four vitals, phone, cameras and the agent, on one screen.
capabilities.agent: Reads the same catalogue; every number says where it came from.
capabilities.notes: Tiles draw 'Not on this car' or 'Waiting for the car', never a stand-in zero.

capabilities.title: Arrange Home by hand
capabilities.user: Drag cards and resize them, per orientation, while parked.
capabilities.agent: Saves a validated layout on request.

capabilities.title: Vehicle: the X-ray car and its systems
capabilities.user: The car's state at a glance, with callouts that point at real systems.
capabilities.agent: Reads the systems summary and opens the right sub-page.
capabilities.notes: Task 8 of the foundation plan.

capabilities.title: The designed palette and type
capabilities.user: A look designed for a dark cabin, not borrowed from the desktop.
capabilities.agent: Reads colours off the live document.

capabilities.title: Every screen says where its numbers came from
capabilities.user: Never mistake simulated data for my car's.
capabilities.agent: Reads the same provenance the badge shows.

capabilities.title: Looks as folders
capabilities.user: Pick a look: palette, logo and texture together, including the chrome and carbon-fibre logos.
capabilities.agent: Installs a look folder and switches to it.
capabilities.notes: Decided 2026-09-27/28. Logos from the owner.

capabilities.title: The car's own picture, kept out of git
capabilities.user: My car on screen, badge and all.
capabilities.agent: Checks the private asset is present and falls back to a placeholder.
capabilities.notes: Honda-badged art stays out of the public repository.

capabilities.title: A 3D model of my own car
capabilities.user: Turn the car on screen, and see where a fault is on it.
capabilities.agent: Loads the model and anchors callouts to it.
capabilities.notes: The viewer exists and contains no car geometry; three.js is not vendored. Photogrammetry of the owner's car is the recommended source.

capabilities.title: Themes I build
capabilities.user: Make a palette for glare or for night, and keep it.
capabilities.agent: Saves and applies a theme.

capabilities.title: Effects driven by the car
capabilities.user: Motion that means something: stars that stretch with speed.
capabilities.agent: Switches effect on request, parked.

capabilities.title: Drive mode
capabilities.user: Few numbers, huge, readable in under a second.
capabilities.agent: Opens it when the car moves.

capabilities.title: A boot screen that says what it waits for
capabilities.user: Know whether it is starting or stuck.
capabilities.agent: Reads the same waiting reason.

capabilities.title: A contract for car screens
capabilities.user: Plugins I already use on the desktop, working on a drive.
capabilities.agent: Builds against one entry point, the design tokens, and the driving state it is given.
capabilities.notes: Supports Omarchy's full-screen `panel` kind first (approved 2026-09-28). Omarchy shell plugins are QML with a manifest of kinds (bar, bar-widget, panel, overlay, menu, service); OmaCar screens are ES modules, so the contract bridges the two for that kind before any other.

capabilities.title: Driving-safety rules the app enforces
capabilities.user: Any plugin is safe to glance at while driving, whoever wrote it.
capabilities.agent: Follows the rules: glanceable only, no text entry, minimum targets, no new motion, and write or actuate greyed out while moving.
capabilities.notes: Enforced by the host, not requested of the plugin. Writes and actuation while moving are refused for good; the other rules are defaults the owner can accept a warning to relax (decided 2026-09-28). See 'Plugin safety rules' in doc/ROADMAP.md.

capabilities.title: One look across every plugin
capabilities.user: A drive looks like one product whatever the plugins are.
capabilities.agent: Reads the active look's tokens and type from the host.
capabilities.notes: lib/theme.py already maps Omarchy's theme onto the app's tokens; the bridge runs the other way too.

capabilities.title: Which Omarchy plugins can work in a car
capabilities.user: Know which of the plugins I use are worth bringing along.
capabilities.agent: Analyses each plugin's kinds, inputs and motion against the safety rules.
capabilities.notes: Two sources: the first-party set in /usr/share/omarchy/shell/plugins, and the community directory at omarchyplugins.com (checked 2026-09-28).

capabilities.title: Plugin authors ship a car version
capabilities.user: My favourite plugin has an OmaCar screen.
capabilities.agent: Adds a car entry point to an existing Omarchy plugin.

capabilities.title: A review checklist before a plugin is offered
capabilities.user: Trust that a listed car plugin follows the rules.
capabilities.agent: Runs the checklist, including the safety rules, before suggesting a plugin.
capabilities.notes: A checklist, not a guarantee; a plugin is still code the owner runs.

capabilities.title: Find and install car plugins in the app
capabilities.user: Browse car-ready plugins and install one while parked.
capabilities.agent: Installs a plugin the owner picked, and nothing else.
capabilities.notes: Installing is refused while moving.

capabilities.title: Plugins that cannot reach past their permissions
capabilities.user: A broken or hostile plugin cannot touch my car.
capabilities.agent: Runs within the permissions it declared.
capabilities.notes: QML plugins run in the shell's process and cannot be sandboxed there; web views could run on a separate origin. Today there is no sandbox, and the docs say so.
